did_you_know.text: Did you know? According to the chapter, all Israel gathered around David at Hebron and acknowledged their close relationship with him, saying, “Look, we are your own flesh and blood.”
Did you know? The elders of Israel made a covenant with David before the LORD, and afterward anointed him king over Israel, in accordance with the word of the LORD spoken through Samuel.
Did you know? David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, Jerusalem, and after he lived in the stronghold, the city was called “the City of David.”
Did you know? The chapter describes David’s growing strength with the words, “David became stronger and stronger,” and adds that the LORD of Hosts was with him.
Did you know? Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, who was among David’s mighty warriors, struck down three hundred men in a single battle with his spear.
Did you know? Eleazar son of Dodo stood with David against the Philistines in a field full of barley, even though the people fled from the enemy.
Did you know? Three of David’s mighty warriors broke through the Philistine camp to draw water for him from the well of Bethlehem, which was near the gate.
Did you know? David would not drink the water the warriors brought him; instead, he poured it out before the LORD because he regarded it as the lifeblood of the men who had risked their lives.

Did you know? Benaiah son of Jehoiada became famous for several acts of bravery: he struck down two of Moab’s champions, climbed down into a pit and killed a lion on a snowy day, and defeated a large Egyptian warrior.
Did you know? Uriah the Hittite is also mentioned in the list of David’s mighty warriors, alongside warriors identified by their places of origin or affiliation.
